title: After Tokens: controlled narrow-viewport geometry audit
status: Engineering observation of one recorded trace; not reader validation or a physical iPhone benchmark.

after.revision: working implementation on 2026-09-09 after release-animation cancellation; before final editorial and accessibility refinements

metricDefinitions.identicalCommittedGlyph: First nonspace character DOM Range of committed ink, matched on source-position/character-offset key and identical current text between successive animation frames. Coordinates are relative to the answer root.
metricDefinitions.releasedGlyph: The same matched glyph only when marked released in both samples. The old renderer uses its released passage spans.
metricDefinitions.positionBox: First client rectangle of a source-position unit or its current text layer; includes drafts, register and text changes. These are diagnostic geometry metrics, not identical-word movement.
metricDefinitions.remounts: A matched source position has a different DOM element in the next observed frame.
metricDefinitions.blurredOrFadedCommittedFrames: At least one observed committed cell or ink layer has computed opacity below 0.99 or blur above 0.2 px in that frame.
metricDefinitions.frameGaps: Observed requestAnimationFrame gaps above 34 ms. Machine-specific diagnostics; not a general performance claim.

conclusions: The new implementation produced zero observed source-position remounts and zero blurred/faded committed-text frames in this sample.
Released glyphs remained stationary across 58,432 matched samples after the release-animation cancellation fix.
The largest identical committed-glyph displacement was 280.5645053287936 px after versus 276.53115111875275 px before. The worst provisional wrap was not improved.
The p99 displacement was 2 px after versus 2.484375 px before; differing glyph/sample populations prevent treating that difference as a controlled reader or aggregate performance result.
Both sampled recordings completed with no horizontal page overflow. This does not establish results for every trace or a physical iPhone.
caveats: Single run per condition, one trace, one browser and one viewport.
The two implementations use different word/token grouping, so glyph sample counts differ; inspect both counts alongside quantiles.
Zero released movement is supported by nonzero released samples; it is not an empty-selector result.
Earlier exploratory 12-second and four-surface runs are excluded from this comparison. The old embedded preview used 2x playback, so it is not a matched-clock comparator.
Large provisional cross-line changes remain. No claim that jitter is eliminated or that reading comfort, comprehension, dopamine or trust improved.
Raw per-frame logs are retained outside the repository; this file contains their exact summaries.
